---
name: project-cart-merge-mechanics
description: SFCC basket merge takes higher-of-two by default, not sum; no Zimmermann code merges at all, and the passwordless sign-in route drops it
metadata:
  type: project
---

Verified 2026-09-16 against `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` types and the base template.

**`mergeBasket`'s `productItemMergeMode`** is `higher_quantity` (default) | `sum_quantities` |
`saved_quantity` | `separate_item`. Default means **guest 2 + account 2 → 2, not 4** — quantities
never sum unless the mode is passed explicitly, and it can only be passed at the call site.

**Same-product matching** requires all of: shipment · productId · option values · wishlist
reference · inventory list id · gift flag & message · ad-hoc price adjustments. Any mismatch
copies the item to a **new line item** instead of merging — so one SKU can exceed a per-order cap
across two lines without either line doing so. For Zimmermann the realistic differentiators are
Collect in Boutique (separate shipment) and boutique vs warehouse inventory lists.

**Four base call sites**, all passing only `createDestinationBasket: true`: `hooks/use-auth-modal`,
`pages/login`, `pages/social-login-redirect`, `pages/checkout/partials/contact-info`. The merge is
deliberately **login-only, not register** — a new customer's guest basket simply becomes theirs.

**No Zimmermann code calls `mergeBasket`**, and `commerce-sdk-react` does not auto-merge (it only
defines the mutation). Of `useWishlistAuthDrawer`'s three routes: social redirects through the base
page that merges; create-account correctly skips it; **passwordless OTP merges nothing** — so a
recurring shopper signing in that way has their guest basket orphaned and **loses their items**.
Code-inferred, not yet observed live — prove it before filing.

**Why:** any cart/checkout work touching sign-in inherits this. Assuming the server sums, or
assuming a merge happens at all, both produce silently wrong baskets.

**How to apply:** check what mode a merge call passes before reasoning about quantities, and treat
"a guest signed in" as "the basket may have been orphaned" until the passwordless gap is fixed.
Related: [[project-cart-bundle-decisions]], [[project-max-order-quantity]].
EOF

Written down in two places.

## `.claude/session-notes.md` — 538 lines

Gitignored, so it can't be committed by accident, and the session-start skill reads it automatically next session. Ten sections:

1. **The bundle** — the 7 cards, the staged-PR-not-mega-PR decision and why, plus the `cart` e2e area gap
2. **Verified findings** — 15 of them, each with its evidence and its caveats: the missing `maxOrderQuantity`, the merge mode default and match criteria, all four base call sites, the passwordless defect, `PendingWishlistIntent`'s missing payload, the 24px target size and why it's deliberate, `checkoutOwner`, the empty-state precedent, the WCAG-annotation house pattern
3. **The reading correction** — cross-references are pointers, not gates; the three I got wrong
4. **Per-card decisions** — every AC adjudicated, with the rejected alternatives and why they were rejected
5. **Cross-story interactions** — the 250/272 weld, the 275-vs-250 button-state question
6. **The prerequisite** — verify then file the merge defect
7. **Five Jira comments to post**
8. **Four follow-up stories to file**
9. **Build order** — fresh branch, copy-first, 315 standalone first
10. **Still unverified** — Figma unopened, the defect code-inferred only, the probe was dev-only and two products, SFCC-318 unconfirmed, and the two decisions you haven't made yet

## Four memory entries

So the expensive findings don't need re-deriving: the cart merge mechanics, the max-order-quantity contradiction, the bundle record pointer, and one small one that'll save time every session — **ACs live in `customfield_10231`, not the description**, and sometimes come back as ADF.

---

Two decisions still open, both noted in §10:

- **SFCC-270** — override base `product-item` (Tier 2, Squad B, API-compatible default export) or build a new `ZimmCartItem` organism (Squad A, but the wishlist page keeps base styling)
- **SFCC-275** — does 315 host the button group in the interim, or does it ship built-but-invisible until 816

And Figma hasn't been opened for any of the seven.

content.text:
## 1. SFCC-270 — override base `product-item`, or build a new one?

**What happens if you override it.** Salesforce's `product-item` is used in three places: the cart page, the account wishlist page, and a list component. Put a file at the override path and *all three* start rendering yours. So yours has to accept every prop the original did — miss one and you break a page you weren't working on. It's also Squad B's file under the Tier 2 rules, so you'd need their review on a Squad A cart ticket.

**The thing that settles it:** you aren't overriding Salesforce's cart page at all. SFCC-315 is a drawer — a brand new component. Salesforce's cart page never renders. So `product-item`'s whole job as "the thing the cart page draws" is irrelevant to you.

Overriding it would mean taking on prop-compatibility with three things you don't use, plus a cross-squad review, to style a wishlist page that isn't in this sprint.

**Recommendation: build a new `ZimmCartItem` organism.** No compatibility constraint, stays in your lane, matches the `ui-kits/organisms/` structure already agreed.

Build it as a genuinely reusable organism rather than something cart-shaped, so when someone does the account wishlist page they adopt the same one. That turns "two components that look different" into "one component not adopted everywhere yet" — a much better problem to have.

## 2. SFCC-275 — does the drawer host the button group now?

**What happens if it doesn't.** You'd ship a cart drawer with line items, a working quantity stepper, remove, and move-to-wishlist — and **no way to check out.** Verifiable in Storybook, useless to a shopper in dev or SIT. That's a cart nobody can buy from.

**Why hosting it is cheap.** When SFCC-816 arrives it's the summary container that wraps the button group. Moving a component from "the drawer draws it" to "the summary inside the drawer draws it" is a small structural change, not a rebuild. You're not throwing work away.

**Recommendation: 315 hosts it now, 816 takes over hosting later.** The cart actually functions in the environments in the meantime, which matters more than a tidy component hierarchy you'll reshuffle in a fortnight anyway.

## 3. Figma — open it when?

**Not a decision about whether, only about when.** Four cards' ACs say "in line with Figma specifications" — 315, 270, 795 and 275. You cannot build responsive breakpoints or exact states without it.

**But it isn't a planning input, it's an implementation input.** Scope is settled now; Figma tells you spacing, sizing and state detail.

**One real risk though, and it's happened here before.** Figma has previously carried scope the cards didn't mention — the f2r product-detail-options prototype turned out to include a size dropdown, a wishlist button, a find-in-boutique link and accordions, none of which any card had asked for.

**Recommendation: open it as the first act of the build session, before locking the step list** — and go in expecting it might add items rather than just confirm numbers. Not now: planning's done, and opening it now restarts a long session on a different axis while you're still holding the whole card set in your head.

One thing to carry in when you do: Figma TEXT nodes measure cap-height, so their numbers aren't directly comparable to CSS. Frames and instances are real boxes and are comparable. And there are two Figma files — don't cross-compare between them.

content.text:
Different job entirely — same product data, opposite shape.

**`ZimmProductCard`** (yours — an organism, with `zimmProductCardMedia` + `zimmProductCardContent` molecules over a `zimmMediaTile` atom) is a **browse card**:

- Vertical — image on top, content below
- Three variations: **PLP, Home, Wishlist**, driven by a `VARIATION_CONFIG` of visibility toggles — `showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showSizeChips`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`, `showRemove`, `hideBagOnMobile`
- Its media molecule is a **gallery**: hover crossfade between two images, desktop prev/next arrows, a touch slide indicator, multi-image paging
- Job: show a product you *might* want, and get it into your bag

**Base `product-item`** is a **line-item row**:

- Horizontal — image left, details right. 270's AC says it outright: *"the product name is displayed to the right of the image"*
- One static thumbnail. No gallery, no hover reveal
- Quantity stepper with `+`/`–`, Remove and Wishlist as underlined text links beneath it, Was/Now pricing, error and warning messages under the stepper
- Job: show a product you *already have*, and change how much of it you have

## Why not just add a fourth variation?

Because `VARIATION_CONFIG` is a **visibility-toggle system inside one layout**. It decides what shows and what appears on hover. It isn't a layout switcher.

A cart row flips the axis, deletes the gallery, and adds controls the card has no slot for. Making it variation four means the config grows layout-direction switches and the fourth branch of that discriminated union looks nothing like the other three.

Worth noting the card has *already* crossed into "things you own" — the Wishlist variation has `showRemove`. The line isn't owned-vs-browsable. It's that Zimmermann's wishlist is a **grid of cards** and the cart is a **list of rows**.

## Correcting what I said earlier

I suggested reusing `zimmProductCardMedia`. Having read it — **don't.** It's a gallery: hover crossfade, arrows, paging. The cart wants a single static thumbnail, and pulling that molecule in drags all of it along.

What *is* worth reusing: `zimmProductCardShared.ts`'s `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and `DESKTOP_QUERY`, and `zimmMediaTile` if it's a plain image tile underneath.

So the recommendation holds — new `ZimmCartItem` organism — but expect reuse at the atom and shared-constant level, not the molecule level.

content.text:
Narrower than I said, and it changes the reasoning. Accurate map:

```
pages/cart  →  components/product-item-list  →  components/product-item
pages/account/wishlist  →  components/product-item          (direct)
```

**That's all.** Two chains. My earlier "three consumers" was a substring false positive — I'd grepped `components/product-item`, which also matches `product-item-list`. The cart reaches it only transitively.

**And checkout doesn't use it at all.** There are two separate line-item systems in the base:

| System | What it does | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `product-item` | Full interactive row — quantity picker, remove, wishlist, bonus products | cart page, account wishlist |
| `item-variant/*` | Read-only composition — `ItemVariantProvider` + `item-image`, `item-name`, `item-attributes`, `item-price` | `order-summary`, so checkout and any summary listing |

I'd speculated checkout "typically" used `product-item-list`. It doesn't.

## What that means for the decision

The blast-radius argument shrinks: overriding would touch base cart (not in your render path — you're building a drawer) and the account wishlist page. One page you'd actually affect, not three.

But two better arguments replace it:

**The bridge pattern makes an override the wrong shape.** `overrideStyling.md` requires that when a component is used internally by SFCC's own base components, the override's **default export stays a faithful, undecorated port** with the full original prop surface, and Zimmermann styling goes behind a *named* export. So you'd be building base's row *and* your Figma row inside one file — a port you don't need plus the thing you do.

**And the wishlist page doesn't want a cart row anyway.** Zimmermann's wishlist is a grid, and `ZimmProductCard` already has `variation: 'wishlist'` with `showRemove` built. So "overriding `product-item` styles the wishlist page for free" was solving a problem that's already solved a different way — that page's future is `ZimmProductCard`, not a line-item row.

So: **new `ZimmCartItem` organism**, and the only real reason to have considered otherwise turns out not to apply.

Accurate consumer map — **two chains only**:
```

pages/account/wishlist  ->  components/product-item          (direct)
```
Checkout does **not** use it. The base has two separate line-item systems: `product-item` (the full
interactive row) and `item-variant/*` (a read-only composition used by `order-summary`, i.e. the

`index.jsx` (7.4 KB), `bonus-product-quantity.jsx` (1.5 KB), `product-quantity-picker.jsx` (3.4 KB),
each to `.tsx`. Base's own `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` are not copied — write our own.

**The finding that changes the size of the job:** `product-item/index.jsx` renders its visible content
through **five more base components** — `components/item-variant` plus `item-variant/item-image`,
`item-name`, `item-attributes`, `item-price`. So overriding `product-item` gives you the row's
*structure and controls*; the *content pieces* still come from `item-variant/*`. Styling those to
Figma means either overriding `item-variant/*` too — which also changes `order-summary`, and
therefore the checkout summaries — or not using them inside our override and composing the content
ourselves. **Decide this before starting: it is the difference between a 3-file override and an
8-file one with checkout blast radius.**

**`shared/ui` barrel trap applies.** `product-item/index.jsx` imports from `components/shared/ui`.
Per the known trap, overriding an individual `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing — 208 base files
import the barrel, so only overriding the barrel itself has any effect.

**Bridge-pattern requirement:** because `product-item` is used internally by base components, the
override's **default export must stay API-compatible** (full original prop surface) so
`product-item-list` and the wishlist page keep working. Per `overrideStyling.md`, put brand styling
in a **theme recipe**, not a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't need the second
export that `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

**Governance:** `overrides/app/components/product-item/` is **Tier 2, Squad B-owned (notify Squad A)**
per `protectedFiles.md`. CODEOWNERS will request Squad B's review on a Squad A ticket.

**Interim consequence, low risk:** while the account wishlist page still consumes `product-item`, our
override's styling reaches it too. `overrides/app/pages/` contains no account pages at all — account
is entirely base and unstyled today — so the exposure is minimal until the wishlist migration lands."""

s = s.replace(old, new)

s = s.replace("- No decision yet on 270's override-vs-new-organism question.\n", "")
s = s.replace(
  "- No decision yet on whether 315 hosts 275's button group in the interim.",
  "- **Open:** whether the override also takes over `item-variant/*` (3-file vs 8-file scope, see §4 SFCC-270)."
)

p.write_text(s)

Recorded. Your decision on `product-item` is in as decided; the other two are marked recommended-but-unconfirmed, since you only answered the first one.

## What overriding `product-item` actually involves

**Copy-first is 3 files** from `retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/` — `index.jsx` (7.4 KB), `bonus-product-quantity.jsx` (1.5 KB), `product-quantity-picker.jsx` (3.4 KB), each to `.tsx`. Base's own tests don't get copied; we write our own.

**But here's the thing that changes the size of the job.** `product-item/index.jsx` renders its visible content through **five more base components**:

```
components/item-variant
components/item-variant/item-image
components/item-variant/item-name
components/item-variant/item-attributes
components/item-variant/item-price
```

So overriding `product-item` gives you the row's **structure and controls** — the quantity picker, remove, wishlist, bonus-product handling. The **content itself** — image, name, colour/size attributes, price — still comes from `item-variant/*`.

Getting those to Figma means one of two things, and they're very different in size:

- **Override `item-variant/*` too** — but `order-summary` uses the same five components, so that reaches the checkout summaries as well. Eight files and a much wider blast radius.
- **Don't use them inside our override** — compose the content ourselves and leave `item-variant/*` alone for `order-summary`. Three files, contained.

That's now the open question in §10, and it's worth deciding before anyone starts.

**Two other things that come with the territory:**

The `shared/ui` barrel trap applies — `product-item/index.jsx` imports from `components/shared/ui`, and overriding an individual `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing.

And the bridge pattern means the override's **default export has to stay API-compatible** with base's full prop surface, so `product-item-list` and the wishlist page keep working until the migration. Brand styling goes in a theme recipe, not a named-export split.

**Governance:** it's Tier 2, Squad B-owned, so CODEOWNERS pulls Squad B into a Squad A ticket.

**One interim side effect, low risk:** until the wishlist page moves to `ZimmProductCard`, our styling reaches it too. `overrides/app/pages/` has no account pages at all — account is entirely base and unstyled today — so there's very little exposed.

---

Still waiting on your word for: **315 hosting the button group**, **Figma timing**, and now **the `item-variant/*` question** — 3 files contained, or 8 with checkout reach.

content.text:
Three things, and one of them I can now answer more firmly than before.

## 1. Does 315 host the button group?

**If no:** you ship a cart drawer with line items, a working stepper, remove and move-to-wishlist — and **no way to check out.** Fine in Storybook, useless to a shopper in dev or SIT.

**Why it's cheap to say yes:** when 816 arrives, it's the summary that wraps the button group. Moving a component from "the drawer draws it" to "the summary inside the drawer draws it" is a small reshuffle, not a rebuild.

**Ask: yes or no.** I'd say yes.

## 2. When does Figma get opened?

Four cards' ACs say "in line with Figma specifications" — 315, 270, 795, 275. You can't build breakpoints or exact states without it.

**The risk isn't skipping it, it's when.** Figma here has previously carried scope no card mentioned — the f2r product-detail-options prototype turned out to include a size dropdown, a wishlist button, a find-in-boutique link and accordions that nothing had asked for. So opening it could *add* work, not just confirm numbers.

**Ask: first act of the build session, before the step list is locked?** That's what I'd do — planning's done, and opening it now restarts a long session on a different axis.

## 3. Three files, or eight?

**What a cart row is made of, in Salesforce's code.** Two layers.

The **row** — the frame, the quantity buttons, the remove and wishlist links. That's `product-item`. You're overriding it.

The **contents** — the picture, the name, the colour and size line, the price. Those are four separate small components the row calls in (`item-variant/*`).

So once you override the row, the things inside it are still Salesforce's.

**Option A — build your own contents inside your row.** Three files. Nothing outside the cart changes.

**Option B — override those four as well.** Eight files. But the checkout order summary uses the same four, so it changes too.

**I checked the thing that made A risky, and it isn't a risk.** `product-item` never renders children passed in by whoever uses it — it wraps only its own content in the context provider, and the wishlist page hands it props only. So swapping the internals cannot break any consumer.

**Ask: A.** Three reasons:

- The cart row is horizontal with its own Figma spacing; the checkout summary is a compact read-only list. Different designs. Making one set of components serve both means the styling has to branch by context, which is exactly what drifts later.
- Checkout isn't built yet. Changing its summary from a cart ticket changes something nobody has specified.
- B's only gain is not writing the content markup twice — but the summary already has a working version, so there's no second write to save.

---

So: **yes to 315 hosting, Figma first thing in the build session, and option A.** Confirm those three and planning is closed.

content.text:
## The issue

**Overriding a shared component can't be scoped.** There's no "use my version only in the cart." Drop a file at the override path and the resolver swaps that module for the whole app.

So the moment you style those four pieces to the cart's Figma, you've also restyled the confirmation page a shopper sees after paying, their order-history detail page, the checkout address cards, and the order summary. None of which has a Zimmermann design yet, none of which is this sprint — and you wouldn't see it, because you'd be looking at the cart.

That's the issue: eleven surfaces changing as a side effect of one.

## But there's a way out I should have found earlier

Those four components **already accept styling as props and spread them onto their own root element:**

```jsx
ItemImage       <Box width="84px" backgroundColor="gray.100" {...props}>
ItemAttributes  <Stack spacing={1.5} flex={1} {...props}>
ItemPrice       {...props}
```

Defaults first, spread after — so a caller wins. That's exactly how `order-summary` already sets its own sizing with `width="80px" mr={2}`.

**So the cart row can pass Zimmermann tokens in and leave the components alone.** No override, no blast radius, no duplicated markup. Which also means the raw Chakra values in there (`gray.100`, `84px`) get replaced by `var(--zimm-*)` at the call site, which is the pattern the styling rules want anyway.

## One exception, and it's a one-line fix

`ItemName` is the odd one out:

```jsx
<Link {...props} color="black.600" to={...}>
```

The spread comes **before** `color`, so `color="black.600"` always wins and a caller can't override it.

That single file needs a surgical override — move the spread after the colour. No base caller passes `color`, so nothing outside the cart changes at all; it just stops being locked.

## Revised recommendation

**4 files, not 8:** the three `product-item` files plus `item-variant/item-name.jsx`.

The cart row uses base `item-variant/*` and passes Zimmermann tokens as props. Nothing outside the cart changes visually. And when checkout and confirmation eventually get designed, they do the same thing from their own call sites — which is better than inheriting cart styling they never asked for.

Worth re-deciding on that basis rather than on the eight-file choice.

I called B "restyling eleven things nobody asked for." That was wrong. content.text: Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/figma/2.2.111/skills/figma-design-to-code # Implement a Figma Design as Code (Design → Code) Use this skill to turn a Figma design into code in a target codebase. This is the **read-FROM-Figma** direction: pull design context out of Figma with `get_design_context`, then adapt it into the project's real stack. For the reverse direction — building or updating a design *in* Figma from code — use [figma-generate-design](../figma-generate-design/SKILL.md) instead. This skill owns the **workflow** for design-to-code. Parameter mechanics (nodeId / fileKey / branchKey extraction, URL parsing, `format`/`query` options, response shape) live on the `get_design_context` tool description itself — follow them there. **Always include `figma-design-to-code` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `get_design_context`. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-design-to-code`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution. ## Direction and Scope - You MUST use this skill for design → code: implementing, translating, or porting a Figma node into code. - You MUST NOT use this skill to write to Figma. ## Workflow ### 1. Call get_design_context first - You MUST call `get_design_context` on the target node before writing any code. It is your primary tool — a single call returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual hints. - You MUST NOT reach for `get_metadata` or `get_screenshot` as a substitute. Use them only to orient (e.g. picking a node) or to validate, not in place of `get_design_context`. ### 2. Treat the output as a reference, not final code - The returned code is React + Tailwind enriched with hints. You MUST treat it as a REFERENCE, not as final code to paste verbatim. - You MUST adapt it to the target project's language, framework, component library, styling system, and conventions. Match the surrounding code. ### 3. Reuse what the project already has - Before writing new code, You MUST check the target project for existing components, layout patterns, and design tokens that match the design intent. - You MUST reuse the project's existing components and tokens instead of generating new equivalents from scratch. ### 4. Honor the response hints by priority Apply the hints in this order — earlier sources override later ones: 1. **Code Connect snippets** → use the mapped codebase component directly. 2. **Component documentation links** → follow them for usage and guidelines. 3. **Design annotations** → follow any designer notes or constraints. 4. **Design tokens (CSS variables)** → map them to the project's token system. 5. **Raw hex / absolute positioning** → loosely structured; lean on the screenshot for intent. ### 5. Reproduce images and icons faithfully Images and icons come back as `` elements whose `src` is a remote asset URL (`https://.../api/mcp/asset/...`). Apply these rules as you write the code: - **Render every icon/image from its exported asset.** Never hand-write or inline `` to fill it (`100%` or fixed px) — never `auto`, which blows the image up to its intrinsic size. ## Error Recovery - On a `get_design_context` error, STOP and read the message before retrying. - If the design URL has no `node-id` (a file-only URL), ask the user for a node-specific URL — You MUST NOT guess or pass an empty `nodeId`. - On a timeout, retry against a smaller node or selection. - You MUST NOT silently fall back to hand-writing the screen from the screenshot alone when `get_design_context` can still provide context.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_design_context
entries.description:
Get design context for a Figma node — the primary tool for design-to-code workflows. Returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual metadata that must be adapted to the target project. 

IMPORTANT: You MUST load figma-design-to-code guidance BEFORE calling this tool. Prefer the /figma-design-to-code skill if available; otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md MCP resource. 

NEVER call this tool without loading that guidance first — skipping it produces code that ignores the target project's existing components, design tokens, and conventions.

Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the node id and file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2` and the fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName then use the makeFileKey to identify the Figma Make file. Only for Figma Make files (URLs containing `/make/`), and only when calling get_design_context, assume the nodeId is `0:1`. The response will contain a code string and a JSON of download URLs for the assets referenced in the code. It will also include a screenshot of the node for context by default.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

clientLanguages.description: A comma separated list of programming languages used by the client in the current context in string form, e.g. `javascript`, `html,css,typescript`, etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which languages are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess.

clientFrameworks.description: A comma separated list of frameworks used by the client in the current context, e.g. `react`, `vue`, `django` etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which frameworks are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess

forceCode.description: Whether code should always be returned, instead of returning just metadata if the output size is too large. Only set this when the user directly requests to force the code.

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether Code Connect should be used to get the design context. Only set this when the user directly requests to disable Code Connect.

skillNames.description: A comma-separated list of Figma skill names being followed, if any (e.g. "figma-design-to-code", "figma-design-to-code,figma-code-connect"). Only pass this when explicitly instructed to by skill documentation. Used for logging purposes. If the skill was loaded via a skill-content MCP resource, prefix the skill name with "resource:". (e.g. "resource:figma-design-to-code", "resource:figma-design-to-code,resource:figma-code-connect")

excludeScreenshot.description: Whether to exclude the screenshot of the design from the response. IMPORTANT: it is not recommended to exclude screenshots. Only set this to true if the user has explicitly requested it or you are trying to preserve context.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_metadata
entries.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_screenshot
entries.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`. Only set `enableBase64Response: true` when the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests); when set, an inline base64 image entry is appended to the response in addition to the URL and curl instructions. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

contentsOnly.description: When true, renders the node in isolation — floating/overlapping content (e.g. connectors parented to the page that visually sit above a section) is excluded. Defaults to false so screenshots match what the user sees on the canvas. Only set to true if the caller specifically needs the isolated render.

enableBase64Response.description: When true, the response also includes the screenshot inline as a base64-encoded image entry, in addition to the short-lived URL and curl instructions. Defaults to false. Set to true ONLY if the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests)

maxDimension.description: Optional. Maximum pixel size of the longer edge of the rendered screenshot — the server scales the node so that max(width, height) ≤ maxDimension while preserving aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024. Must be a positive integer; values above 65536 are rejected. Increase when the agent will visually inspect fine detail; decrease for thumbnails or to save context.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_variable_defs
entries.description: Get variable definitions for a given node id. E.g. {'icon/default/secondary': #949494}Variables are reusable values that can be applied to all kinds of design properties, such as fonts, colors, sizes and spacings. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Extract the node id from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This remote tool requires a concrete node target. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

- Default/Price        : size350 / lh450 / ls 0 / w500
- Default/Caption-strong: size300 / lh450 / ls 0 / w500
- Default/Link-sm      : size300 / lh350 / ls negative-100 / w500

## FLAGS RAISED SO FAR
1. **Stepper icons are 12x12px in Figma.** Our ZimmButton `icon` size is 24px
   (deliberate, WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8). SFCC-795's AC demands 44x44.
   => THREE different numbers: Figma 12, atom 24, AC 44. As drawn there is no
   padded hit area around the 12px icon.
2. `gap-[25px]` in Item Actions is an untokenised raw value -> will trip `npm run audit:tokens`.
3. SFCC-270 has separate ACs for "colour is displayed" and "size is displayed", but the
   design renders them as a single combined string. Two ACs, one element.
4. `PdpPrice` has a `state` prop (default "Default") -> promotional Was/Now is a variant of it.

Checkpoint — core components of our delivery are pulled. Five things worth your attention now, before I work through the remaining state groups.

## 1. The 44px conflict just resolved itself — against the AC

Figma has an **explicitly named `touchTarget` node, sized exactly 24px**, wrapping a 20px icon in the message component.

So: **Figma says 24. Our `ZimmButton` says 24. WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 says 24. SFCC-795's AC says 44.** The AC is the outlier against both the design system *and* the implementation — not a design-vs-standard tension at all. That makes the annotate-and-log call much easier to defend.

## 2. But the stepper has no touch target at all

The cart item's `Icon_minus` / `Icon_plus` are **12×12px with no `touchTarget` wrapper** — unlike the message icon, which has one. That reads as a design inconsistency rather than intent. Worth putting to the designer: should the stepper icons get the same 24px wrapper?

## 3. "CART MERGE" is actually 250's post-merge state

The frame is named `cart/drawer/large/**error**`, composition identical to default, and the only difference is the message band reading:

> **"An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity"**

## 4. The message band is reserved even when empty

Designer annotation on the default node:

> *"When there are no errors in cart, there will still be space for the errors to prevent the cart changing position depending on errors"*

So the 52px band always occupies its space. **SFCC-315 has to reserve it now**, even though 404 fills it later — otherwise adding 404 causes a layout shift. That's new scope for 315, small but real.

## 5. Two things in the cart design that aren't in our seven cards

`Promotion-code` (SFCC-191, Squad B, Bianca) sits **inside** the Totals-summary we're putting the button group into — a coordination point. And there's a **`Recommended-for-you` rail** at 430×231, which is Einstein-powered, and Einstein is Not Deployed on all eight sites.

## Also confirmed, cleanly

Button group maps exactly to our atoms — `h-52` = `actionSizes.height.lg`, `px-32` = `paddingX.lg`, `gap-16` = `actionSizes.gap`, primary `#191919` solid, secondary outlined. No atom gap for 275. The drawer is a **fixed 1186px** panel on desktop, 659.2 on tablet, full-width on mobile.

**Big one.** Another designer rule annotation, and it reshapes SFCC-404:

> *"Error messages are compiled into one overarching message... If there are multiple errors within cart, the message will call out how many errors the user needs to fix before proceeding. When a customer reduces an error, the quantity in the error message also goes down; Errors should always stay at the top when multiple messages are stacked"*

So errors **aggregate into one counted message** with a live count, pinned to top. Note the plural forms too — "There **is 1** item... that **requires** action" vs "There **are 2** items... that **require** action" — full ICU pluralisation, not just a number swap.

## SFCC-404 IS NOT A SIMPLE BANNER — full behavioural model from 3 designer annotations

**Annotation 1 (stacked errors, node 9323:102373):**
> "Error messages are compiled into one overarching message. This message will be high-level, to
>  encourage users to scroll within their cart and identify where they need to resolve the errors.
>  If there are multiple errors within cart, the message will call out how many errors the user
>  needs to fix before proceeding. When a customer reduces an error, the quantity in the error
>  message also goes down; Errors should always stay at the top when multiple messages are stacked"

**Annotation 2 (wishlist success, node 9323:97139):**
> "Only one success message can be shown at a time... the white container stays fixed, the old
>  success message will fade, then the new success message will fade into the container"

**Annotation 3 (warnings hidden, node 9323:103807):**
> "No warnings are to be shown at the cart level when a success or error message is present.
>  This reduces the clutter when there are multiple messages stacked"

**Annotation 4 (default, node 9323:94689):**
> "When there are no errors in cart, there will still be space for the errors to prevent the cart
>  changing position depending on errors"

### Resulting model
- 3 severity variants: error (Icon_close, #9c0000) / success (Icon_tick, #2d5a3d) /
  warning (Icon_info_solid, #969696)
- **Errors aggregate into ONE counted message** with a LIVE count that decrements as the shopper
  fixes them. Full ICU pluralisation: "There **is 1** item ... that **requires** action" vs
  "There **are 2** items ... that **require** action"
- **Precedence: errors pinned top; error+success may stack (4px gap); warnings SUPPRESSED whenever
  an error or success is present**
- Success is single-slot with a crossfade, container fixed
- Region reserves min 52px even when empty

=> This is a message *aggregator with severity ordering, live counting and transitions*, not a
   3-variant strip. **My earlier "half a day" estimate when Marcel was deciding whether to pull 404
   forward was wrong by a lot.**

### Stacked-state copy inconsistency
Single success: "**Cloud 91 Small Clutch** added to Wishlist" (product named)
Stacked success: "**Item** added to Wishlist" (generic)
Design drops the product name when stacked. Intentional compaction or inconsistency - ask.

## *** THE DISCLOSURE MESSAGE EXISTS *** (node 9323:105446, WARNINGS SHOWN)
> **"An item in your bag has been reduced to the maximum allowed quantity"**

So there are TWO distinct max-quantity messages in the design:
1. "has **reached** maximum quantity"  -> you are at the cap (CART MERGE state)
2. "has been **reduced to** the maximum allowed quantity" -> **we changed your bag** (WARNINGS SHOWN)

SFCC-250's ACs contain only #1. #2 is the disclosure I raised and Marcel ruled out of scope —
**he ruled on my statement that no such copy existed. That statement was wrong.** The design has it.

Typography differs on this one: `Default/Body 2 Medium` = Futura Round **Medium**/500,
tracking -0.14px, colour `var(--text/muted)` #969696 — vs the other messages' `Default/body2`
regular/400, ls 0, `alias/color/text/subtlest` #969696. Two tokens, same hex. More token drift.

## International (node 9323:65941 / button group I9323:102241;40004371:138266)
Button-group has exactly ONE child: the CHECKOUT button. Apple/Google Pay are **removed, not
hidden** — so 275 AC2's "no white gap" is a plain conditional render. Totals-summary stays 430x857.
EOF

content.text:
Two things you need before I finish the reference-only groups.

## 1. The disclosure message exists. I told you it didn't.

There's a state — WARNINGS SHOWN — whose copy is:

> **"An item in your bag has been reduced to the maximum allowed quantity"**

So the design has **two distinct max-quantity messages**:

| | Copy | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| CART MERGE state | "has **reached** maximum quantity" | you're at the cap |
| WARNINGS SHOWN state | "has been **reduced to** the maximum allowed quantity" | **we changed your bag** |

SFCC-250's ACs only contain the first. You ruled disclosure out of scope — but you ruled on my statement that no message anywhere told the shopper their quantity had been reduced. **That was wrong.** The designer wrote exactly that message.

Not reopening the decision, just correcting the premise it rested on. Worth knowing the copy exists and is specced before you finalise it.

## 2. SFCC-404 is much bigger than I estimated

Four designer annotations across the states define a full behavioural model:

- **Errors aggregate into one counted message** — "There are 2 items in your bag that require action" — with a **live count that decrements** as the shopper resolves them, and full ICU pluralisation ("is 1 item… requires" vs "are 2 items… require")
- **Precedence**: errors pinned to top · error + success may stack (4px gap) · **warnings suppressed entirely whenever an error or success is present**
- **Success is single-slot with a crossfade** — container stays fixed, old message fades out, new fades in
- **Region reserves 52px even when empty**, so the cart never shifts

That's a message aggregator with severity ordering, live counting and transitions — not a strip with three variants. When you were deciding whether to pull 404 forward, I estimated "half a day." **That was wrong by a lot.** Doesn't change the decision to defer it, but it does change what next sprint costs you.

## Smaller things from this batch

- **International**: express buttons are *removed*, not hidden — AC2's "no white gap" is a plain conditional render
- **Already-in-wishlist** uses the **warning** variant, not an error banner as AC6 says, and its copy is generic ("An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist") rather than product-specific
- **Stacked success drops the product name** — "Item added to Wishlist" vs "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" when alone. Inconsistency or intentional compaction; worth asking

Carrying on with the six reference-only groups — Shop the Look, Voucher, Promo code, Replace promo, and the two gift-card states.

---

# 11. Figma — cart design specs (pulled 2026-09-16)

File `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (Zimmermann_Designs). 17 state groups. Raw per-node log kept
separately; this section is the build-relevant consolidation.

## 11.1 Breakpoints and shell

| Frame | Viewport | Drawer panel | Header | Gutter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cart/drawer/xlarge` | 1920x1024 | **1186 fixed**, x=736 | 84 | 128 (content) / 64 (header) |
| `cart/drawer/large` | 1440x1024 | **1186 fixed**, x=256 | 84 | same — composition IDENTICAL to xlarge |

| `cart/drawer/mobile` | 402x956 | **402 full-width**, 2224 tall (scrolls) | **108** | **32** |

Drawer is a **fixed 1186px panel** on desktop, not a percentage.

```
pdp/drawer                       <- name is a PDP copy artefact, ignore
|- drawer/header          1186x84    pt 40 (space/1000), px 64 (space/1600), row h 44
|- Cart-level-messages    1186x52    px 128 (space/3200), min-h 52  <- SFCC-404
|- drawer-content
   |- Content Container (y+32)
   |  |- Cart Summary     930x857  (x=128)
   |     |- Cart-item-group 360 wide, items 360x198, pitch 246 => 48px gap
   |     |- Totals summary  430 wide (x=500 => 140px gutter)
   |- Zimmermann-benefits 1186x228   <- SFCC-316 (Jhoan, Sprint 5)
```
Mobile collapses to **one column**: items (338w) then totals (338w) with 48px between.

## 11.2 Cart Item (SFCC-270 / 795 / 271 / 272 / 250)

Desktop 360x198 · mobile 338x131 · gift-card variant 226.

| | Desktop | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| root gap / align | 28px (space/700) / items-center | **24px (space/600) / items-start** |
| Image Group | 132x198, object-cover, py 12.655 | **67x100.3, object-contain, py 8.944** |
| Item Details gap | 12px (space/300) | **24px (space/600)** |
| Item Info | flex-col, name above price | **flex-row justify-between** |

- image: aspect **288/432**, bg `alias/color/bg/surface/default` **#f6f4f1**, `mix-blend-multiply`
- product name: **uppercase**, `Default/Product-name` 14px / lh16 / #191919
- price: `Default/Price` 14px / lh18 / #191919, inner gap 8px. `PdpPrice` has a `state` prop —
  promotional Was/Now is a variant of it
- colour + size: **ONE combined string** ("Lilac Sand, One size"), `Default/Caption-strong`
  12px / lh18 / `text/subtle` **#666**, w 200px
  (SFCC-270 has separate ACs for colour and for size — two ACs, one element)
- quantity: gap 12px, **Icon_minus / Icon_plus 12x12px, NO touch-target wrapper**
- actions: gap **25px (RAW, untokenised)**, links h 24 / py 4, **capitalize**, underlined,
  `Default/Link-sm` 12px / lh14 / ls **-0.12px** / `link/default` #191919
- inline message (error/warning) sits **between the stepper and the actions**, w-full,
  `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details gap widens 12 -> 16px.
- disabled steppers ship as **separate greyed SVG assets** (we use OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4)

Copy: fully OOS "This item is unavailable" · partial OOS "Quantity unavailable in this size"

**Gift card variant** (out of scope, but the component API must allow it): no stepper, no actions,
a 5-field label/value block, annotation "Truncate message text when it goes over two lines".
=> build `ZimmCartItem` with the stepper and actions row **optional**. Physical gift cards render
as a standard 198 item; only digital is special.

## 11.3 Cart-level-messages (SFCC-404) — NOT a simple banner

Shell: px 128, bg white, gap 4px between stacked messages, **min-h 52 reserved even when empty**,
`Page-level-message` w **476px** fixed, `Message-container` gap 8px,
**`touchTarget` 24x24 wrapping a 20px icon**, text `Default/body2` (Futura Round regular/400,
14px, lh 18px).

| Variant | Icon | Colour |
|---|---|---|
| Error | `Icon_close` | `text/error` **#9c0000** |
| Success | `Icon_tick` | `text/success` **#2d5a3d** |
| Warning | `Icon_info_solid` | `text/subtlest` **#969696** |

**Four designer annotations define real behaviour no AC mentions:**
1. Empty state still reserves the space "to prevent the cart changing position depending on errors"
2. Errors **aggregate into one counted message** with a **live count that decrements** as the
   shopper resolves them; errors **always stay at the top** when stacked
3. Only **one success at a time**; container stays fixed, old fades out, new fades in
4. **Warnings are suppressed entirely** whenever an error or success is present

=> precedence: error (pinned, aggregated) > success (single-slot, crossfade) > warning (suppressed).
=> full ICU pluralisation: "There **is 1** item ... **requires** action" / "There **are 2** ...
   **require** action".
=> **This is a message aggregator with severity ordering, live counting and transitions.** The
   "half a day" estimate given when deciding whether to pull 404 forward was wrong by a lot.
=> our interim Chakra toast **stacks** by default — a poorer stand-in than assumed, but still
   interim. Reinforces routing every message through one handler.

Copy found: "There is 1 item in your bag that requires action" · "An item in your bag has reached
maximum quantity" · "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" · "An item in your bag already exists
in Wishlist" · "Item added to Wishlist" (stacked — **drops the product name**)

## 11.4 *** DISCLOSURE COPY EXISTS — corrects a decided premise ***

The WARNINGS SHOWN state reads:
> **"An item in your bag has been reduced to the maximum allowed quantity"**

Two distinct max-quantity messages exist:
1. "has **reached** maximum quantity" — at the cap (CART MERGE state)
2. "has been **reduced to** the maximum allowed quantity" — **we changed your bag**

SFCC-250's ACs contain only #1. Disclosure was ruled out of scope **on my statement that no such
copy existed — that statement was wrong.** The decision stands unless Marcel revisits it, but the
premise was false and the copy is specced.

## 11.5 Cart-button-group (SFCC-275)

430x188. Button-group flex-col gap **16px** (space/400). All buttons **h 52**, px **32**
(space/800), min-w 80, w-full.
- Checkout: bg `action/primary/bg/default` **#191919**, text white, **UPPERCASE**, 14px / lh16
- Apple / Google Pay: 1px border `action/secondary/border/default` **#191919**; logos 48x24
  (absolutely positioned in Figma — a compositional shortcut; in code they are button children)

**Verified against our atoms:** h52 == `actionSizes.height.lg`, px32 == `paddingX.lg`,
gap16 == `actionSizes.gap`; ZimmButton `primary` / `secondary` map exactly. No atom gap.
Also confirms the removed `BTN_HEIGHT_LG = 50px` provisional was wrong.

**International:** Button-group has exactly ONE child — express buttons are **removed, not hidden**.
AC2's "no white gap" is a plain conditional render. Totals-summary height unchanged.

## 11.6 Totals-summary (SFCC-274 / 816) — context for our button group

430x857. Rows at y 0/30/60/89/118: Total Items, Shipping, Subtotal, GST, Grand Total.
Label 310w at x=0, value 100w at x=330 (20px gutter). **Currency symbol is its own 8px text node.**
3x Grand Total Container, 2 hidden => regional tax-display variants.
Also contains **Promotion-code** (SFCC-191, Squad B, Bianca — an accordion, border-top #e6e6e6,
header "ADD PROMOTION CODE", 16px chevron) and **Recommended-for-you** 430x231.

`Recommended-for-you` swaps its heading to **"SHOP THE LOOK"** for signed-out shoppers — so a
**non-personalised fallback exists that does not need Einstein** (relevant: Einstein is Not
Deployed on all 8 sites).

## 11.7 Empty bag (SFCC-315 AC2 / SFCC-277)

Layout **changes**, not just copy: Cart-item-group -> 360x157; **Totals summary moves x=500 -> x=0**
and shrinks 430x857 -> **430x263** at y=297. Two columns collapse to one.
- "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY" is in the **header**, not the body
- the body is **Client Services contact copy**: "If you'd like some help, speak to one of our Client
  Services Advisors at: / +61 1800 738 895 / Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM / or
  clientservices@zimmermann.com" (email underlined)
- `Default/Body 1` Futura Round Regular 16px / lh 24 / ls **-0.16px**; paragraph spacing
  `mb-[25px]` (RAW)
- **AU phone number and AU opening hours are hardcoded in the design** — must vary per storefront
  across 8 sites. No AC covers this.

## 11.8 Touch targets — Figma is internally inconsistent

| Element | Wrapper | Icon |
|---|---|---|
| Cart-level-message | named `touchTarget` **24x24** | 20 |
| Recommended-for-you chevrons | **24x24** | 16 |
| drawer/header close | **44h x 24w** | 16 |
| **Cart item stepper +/-** | **none** | **12** |

"44" has provenance (close-button height) but **nothing in the design is 44x44**, which is what
SFCC-795's AC asks for. And the stepper has no touch target at all — 12px, half the 24px the rest
of the system uses. Per the house pattern (`zimmButton.css.ts`): annotate inline citing the
criterion and the source, add to the UI designer's open list, ship. Also **ask the designer whether
the stepper icons should get the same 24px touchTarget** — it reads as an oversight, not intent.

## 11.9 Design-side issues to raise

- stepper icons 12px with no touch target, against a 24px system convention

content.text:
Correct. The glyph stays 12×12; the wrapper is an invisible centred box that only claims pointer area. No background, no border — nothing visible changes about the icon itself.

It's the pattern the design already uses everywhere else:

| Element | Hit area | Visible glyph |
|---|---|---|
| Message icon | 24×24 (named `touchTarget`) | 20 |
| Carousel chevrons | 24×24 | 16 |
| Header close | 44×24 | 16 |
| **Stepper** | **none** | **12** |

So the stepper is the only control in the drawer where the glyph *is* the hit area.

**And we get it almost free.** `ZimmButton`'s `icon` size is already `minW`/`minH: var(--zimm-scale-xl)` = 24px. Its own comment explains why it's `minW`/`minH` and not padding — Chakra's `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0` as a style prop that merges after `__css`, so padding in the recipe is silently dropped, and an earlier `p: 'xs'` rendered 16×16. Using that variant with a 12px glyph gives exactly what you're describing.

## One consequence worth putting to the designer with it

Adding the wrapper changes the **visual** spacing, because a 24px box around a 12px glyph adds 6px of invisible padding each side.

The design is `glyph — 12px gap — qty — 12px gap — glyph`. With wrappers, the apparent gap becomes `6 + gap`. To keep it looking identical at 12px, the coded gap would need to be **6px** — and there's no 6px token. `spacing.ts` jumps `4px (2xs) → 8px (xs) → 12px (s)`.

So: 4px gives 10px apparent, 8px gives 14px apparent. Neither is exactly the design's 12.

Worth asking them as part of the same question — *"if the stepper gets 24px targets, do you want visual parity (needs an off-scale 6px) or token-compliant spacing at 10 or 14?"* Otherwise whoever builds it silently picks one.

content.text:
The codebase already answered it, and consistently with the design — **24px**.

## What's actually there

**24px is the icon-control standard**, as `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` `minW`/`minH`, in four atoms:

```
zimmButton.css.ts:319      minW/minH: var(--zimm-scale-xl)
zimmTextInput.css.ts:174   minWidth/minHeight: var(--zimm-scale-xl)
zimmNavItem.css.ts:16      minHeight: var(--zimm-scale-xl)  // 24px — Figma: h-[24px]
footerNavColumn            minHeight 24px
```

**44px exists too — but it's a row height, not a square target:**

```
zimmDrawer.css.ts:184   "gives the close button its own real 44px row"
zimmDrawer.css.ts:254   "py-24px wrapping a 44px row = 92px total at md+"
zimmTabs.css.ts:31      "Figma's drawer-header-options row is a fixed 44px tall at every
                         breakpoint (desktop, tablet, and mobile frames all measure h-[44px])"
```

That last comment is the same `drawer-header-options` row I measured at 44px in the cart header — so the codebase already documented this and built to it.

## So it isn't 24 *or* 44

They're two different things, and both are already implemented correctly:

- **24px** — the minimum hit area for an icon control
- **44px** — the drawer header row height, with a 24-wide close target centred in it

**SFCC-795's 44×44 conflates the two.** It takes the row height and applies it as a square icon target, which matches nothing in either the design or the code.

**So the stepper follows 24px.** No designer input needed — that's four atoms' worth of precedent, and it's what the cart design's own `touchTarget` node specifies.

**Item 3 comes off the list.** Down to seven, and one more thing: `zimmProductDescription.css.ts` already carries *"Owner: UI designer, batched with the 28px / 44px gap questions"* — so there's an existing designer batch these could join rather than opening a new thread.

| Mobile 402 | full-width | single column | 32px |

The odd decimals are computed fill widths, not specs — so implement tablet as fluid with a 32px gutter, never a hardcoded 659.2.

content.text:
All three settle without the designer. Here they are with what I'd settle on.

## 1. Stepper touch target

**One honest correction first:** 12px isn't strictly a WCAG 2.2 AA failure. SC 2.5.8 has a spacing exception — undersized targets pass if a 24px circle centred on each doesn't intersect another target's circle. Minus-centre to plus-centre is about 43px here, so they clear it. Compliant, just poor.

**Settle it as 24px anyway**, on codebase precedent rather than compliance: four atoms already standardise on `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` `minW`/`minH` — `zimmButton`, `zimmTextInput`, `zimmNavItem`, `footerNavColumn` — and `ZimmButton`'s `icon` variant gives it for free. Figma's own `touchTarget` node is 24. Glyph stays 12px, so nothing looks different.

**And settle the spacing consequence:** apparent gap becomes `6 + coded gap`, and no token gives the 6px needed for exact parity (`spacing.ts` jumps 4 → 8 → 12). Use **`2xs` (4px)** → 10px apparent versus the design's 12px. Two pixels tighter in a stepper gap, annotated. Not worth a designer round-trip.

## 2. Stacked-success product naming

**Settle it: always include the product name.**

- SFCC-272's AC is explicit — `[Product Name]` in every case
- The cards' "figma leading" note reads *"Image for reference (figma leading)"* — it's about visual reference, not overriding AC copy
- One message template instead of two
- 795 already says message text is configurable, and the real surface is 404 next sprint — so this rides with 404 if anyone objects

Changing a string later is trivial. Not worth blocking on.

## 3. Mobile drift

All three settle by arithmetic or by our own proven pattern:

**`px-[128px]` on mobile → 32px.** Proven: the mobile and tablet cart summaries both sit at a 32px gutter. 128 is the desktop value left behind.

**`w-[476px]` vs `w-full` → 476 on desktop, full-width on mobile.** 476px cannot fit a 402px viewport, so `w-full` is correct there and 476 is the desktop constraint. Settled by the numbers.

**Header 108 vs 68 → take 108, the default state's value.** The error-state frames are the ones we've demonstrated are off-pattern — same frames carrying the hardcoded 128px gutter and raw hex colours. When the canonical state and a proven-drifted state disagree, follow the canonical one.

---

So **nothing left for the designer as a blocker.** What I'd still send them is a short FYI — the stepper now has a 24px target, mobile has several hardcoded desktop values, and the warnings-shown state is off-pattern in four ways — batched onto the existing *"28px / 44px gap questions"* thread in `zimmProductDescription.css.ts` rather than opened as a new one.

Want me to record these settlements and then draft that FYI?
